about.title: About me
about.manifesto: I am a physicist. I learned to listen to the atmosphere with radars, magnetometers and electric field sensors, and now I use data and the cloud to anticipate what comes next.
paragraphs: I trained at the National University San Luis Gonzaga in Ica. At CIEASEST, the center that studies solar activity and its effects on Earth, I worked with large volumes of data from real instruments and supervised equipment for the Geophysical Institute of Peru.
That experience led me to data analysis and cloud computing: I trained in Python, SQL and AWS on full scholarships, and led data teams on projects with tight deadlines.

My thesis aims to anticipate lightning by combining electric field networks, satellite and radar. I want to keep doing research in a graduate program and build systems that turn measurements into timely decisions.

thesis.title: Lightning prediction with electric field mill networks
thesis.lead: Lightning usually announces itself: the electric field near the ground changes while a storm charges up. My thesis uses that signal to anticipate strikes and tests whether adding satellite and radar data improves the warning.
thesis.question: Does adding GLM and weather radar data make an electric-field-based warning algorithm more efficient?
thesis.demoTitle: How an electric field warning works
thesis.demoCaption: Illustrative simulation, not real data. When the field crosses the threshold a warning is issued; the time until the strike is the lead time.

data.name: Electric field mills (EFM)
data.text: Ground sensor networks in São Paulo, Brazil: the CRAAM EFMs (Mackenzie Presbyterian University), the Atibaia station and the USP network.

data.name: GOES-GLM
data.text: The Geostationary Lightning Mapper on board the GOES satellites detects lightning light from geostationary orbit.

data.name: Weather radar
data.text: Describes the structure of storm clouds and how they evolve, information that can precede their electrification.

method.name: Baseline
method.text: A warning algorithm that uses only the electric field network.

method.name: Data fusion
method.text: Add the GLM and radar data to the same algorithm.

method.name: Comparison
method.text: Measure whether the warning improves: hits, false alarms and lead time.

thesis.why: Lightning puts people, power grids, airports and outdoor activities at risk. Knowing which data improve the warning helps decide where to invest in sensors and how to combine them.
thesis.note: Project in progress. This page will be updated with results.
